Topics · Is there a God?

Would hurting a child be wrong if all approved?

Neither of us doubts this is wrong. What does that rest on, if not opinion? The answer has a stated limit.

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَإِذَا ٱلْمَوْءُۥدَةُ سُئِلَتْ٨ بِأَىِّ ذَنۢبٍ قُتِلَتْ٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when the girl [who was] buried alive is asked For what sin she was killed

Quran · At-Takwir 81:8-9

﴿وَإِذَا بُشِّرَ أَحَدُهُم بِٱلْأُنثَىٰ ظَلَّ وَجْهُهُۥ مُسْوَدًّا وَهُوَ كَظِيمٌ٥٨ يَتَوَٰرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ مِن سُوٓءِ مَا بُشِّرَ بِهِۦٓ ۚ أَيُمْسِكُهُۥ عَلَىٰ هُونٍ أَمْ يَدُسُّهُۥ فِى ٱلتُّرَابِ ۗ أَلَا سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ٥٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

And when one of them is informed of [the birth of] a female, his face becomes dark, and he suppresses grief. He hides himself from the people because of the ill of which he has been informed. Should he keep it in humiliation or bury it in the ground? Unquestionably, evil is what they decide.

Quran · An-Nahl 16:58-59

This is not a question about whether you are moral. You are. You know this is wrong and you need no book to say so. The question is what that knowing rests on. History has a hard case. A society once accepted burying newborn girls alive. Some saw no wrong in it. This text names that cruelty, and it says the child herself will be asked for what offence she was killed. It does not treat public opinion as settling anything. Was it wrong then, or only unpopular now?

A question for you

When you say this is wrong, what do you mean?

If you sayThat it is really wrong, at all times.
ThenThen wrongness does not depend on anyone's opinion. It leaves what it stands on.
If you sayThat it harms, and harm is bad.
ThenThat is a strong answer. It leaves why harm is bad, when the stronger party does not care.
If you sayThat our society agreed on it.
ThenThen burying that child was not wrong for those who accepted it. That can be said, though few accept it.
If you sayI don't know.
ThenThat does not mean you doubt it is wrong. It means the ground is not yet clear.

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَنَفْسٍ وَمَا سَوَّىٰهَا٧ فَأَلْهَمَهَا فُجُورَهَا وَتَقْوَىٰهَا٨﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [by] the soul and He who proportioned it[1932] And inspired it [with discernment of] its wickedness and its righteousness,

Translator's notes

[1932] i.e., balanced and refined it, creating in it sound tendencies and consciousness.

Quran · Ash-Shams 91:7-8

Translation

(for when Gentiles who don’t have the law do by nature the things of the law, these, not having the law, are a law to themselves, in that they show the work of the law written in their hearts, their conscience testifying with them, and their thoughts among themselves accusing or else excusing them)

Original · Ancient Greek

ὅταν γὰρ ἔθνη τὰ μὴ νόμον ἔχοντα φύσει τὰ τοῦ νόμου ποιῶσιν, οὗτοι νόμον μὴ ἔχοντες ἑαυτοῖς εἰσιν νόμος· οἵτινες ἐνδείκνυνται τὸ ἔργον τοῦ νόμου γραπτὸν ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις αὐτῶν, συμμαρτυρούσης αὐτῶν τῆς συνειδήσεως καὶ μεταξὺ ἀλλήλων τῶν λογισμῶν κατηγορούντων ἢ καὶ ἀπολογουμένων,

Romans · 2:14-15

World English Bible

Here is the proposal. The knowing is built into what a person is. A soul does not need to be taught that cruelty is cruel, as it doesn't need to be taught that it hurts. If so, the moral sense would be a kind of perception: you see something that is there. That is why it can correct a whole society, and why reformers stand against their own people. A preference could not do that. This text says it in a few words. It doesn't say who is good.

A question for you

Is the moral sense more like seeing or more like taste?

If you sayLike seeing. It detects something real.
ThenThen there is something to detect. The question is what, and from where.
If you sayLike taste. It varies among people.
ThenThen burying the child is not truly wrong, you only dislike it. Are you content with that?
If you saySomething else. It evolved in us.
ThenThat explains how it arose, not whether it is true. That difference is taken up elsewhere.

Part 3 of 3

﴿بَلِ ٱلْإِنسَـٰنُ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِۦ بَصِيرَةٌ١٤ وَلَوْ أَلْقَىٰ مَعَاذِيرَهُۥ١٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,[1804] Even if he presents his excuses.

Translator's notes

[1804] As described in 36:65 and 41:20-23.

Quran · Al-Qiyamah 75:14-15

Translation

Before judgment, examine yourself, and in the hour of scrutiny you will find forgiveness. Humble yourself before you get sick. In the time of sins, repent.

Original · Ancient Greek

Πρὸ κρίσεως ἐξέταζε σεαυτόν, καὶ ἐν ὥρᾳ ἐπισκοπῆς εὑρήσεις ἐξιλασμόν. Πρὶν ἀῤῥωστῆσαί σε ταπεινώθητι, καὶ ἐν καιρῷ ἁμαρτημάτων δεῖξον ἐπιστροφήν.

Sirach · 18:20-21

World English Bible

So what makes it wrong? The answer offered: the moral order is real because the source of everything is itself just. A child has a worth no vote can remove, because no vote gave it. You may still ask why that should bind you, and some atheist philosophers hold moral truths with no God. The claim is only that if the torturer is really wrong, something is true of the world that matter alone does not obviously explain. A person, the text adds, is a witness against himself.

A question for you

Which ground seems strongest to you?

If you sayNo ground. It is only what we feel.
ThenThat is consistent. Its price is that the torturer is someone who disagrees, not someone who is wrong.
If you sayMoral truths that need no God.
ThenThat is serious. It has to say what they are and why they bind.
If you sayA just source behind everything.
ThenThat is what the text offers. It has to show that such a source exists.
